title: Tested on 22,188 NSE results, 2019–2026
n_label: 22,188 NSE results from Jul 2019 to Jul 2026
findings: Prices keep drifting after results on NSE. Across 22,188 results, a PEAD score of 7–9 was followed by an average +6.9% against NIFTY 500 over the next 60 sessions (median +2.7%, 56% beat the index), against -0.0% for 0–2. Over 120 sessions: +11.5% vs +0.7%.

It held up in every calendar year tested (8 of 8; t-statistic 10.0 with standard errors clustered by month), in both halves of the sample and in every market-cap band — but it is strongest in smaller companies: PEAD 7–9 under ₹10,000 Cr averaged +8.2%, over ₹50,000 Cr +2.3% (as US studies found, drift lives where attention is thin).

The market under-reacts to results: the first two sessions' move is the strongest single sign of what comes next (Brandt et al.'s announcement-return effect). A reaction of +10% or more vs the index was followed by +5.8% more over 60 sessions; a fall of 6% or more by -0.7%.

Revenue surprises carry as much information as profit surprises (Jegadeesh & Livnat): once both were in the model, revenue added the most. Profit was best measured against the company's own history of yearly changes (standardised unexpected earnings) plus how big the jump is next to the share price.

Result-day volume added almost nothing once the price reaction and the closing strength were known, so it is shown on the card but not scored. Stocks already within 10% of their 52-week high drifted more after good results than beaten-down ones.

Result Quality measures whether the strength lasts. With a score of 85+, next quarter's operating profit was also up on the year 91% of the time, against 40% under 40 — higher in every year tested (8 of 8; t-statistic 35). Those stocks beat NIFTY 500 by +5.0% over 60 sessions and +10.2% over 120 (under 40: +0.1% and +1.1%).

The strongest single quality sign was a margin at its best level in five quarters: next quarter's operating profit rose 86% of the time (otherwise 60%), and the stock did +3.8% vs +1.1% over 60 sessions. Revenue growth and a run of rising quarters came next.

The forensic checks (exceptional gains, a tax rate under 10%, other income above 30% of profit before tax, a net loss) did not move the next 60 days' return much, but they did predict that net-profit growth would not repeat next quarter — which is why they cost Quality points rather than PEAD points.
Both scores together: PEAD 7–9 with Quality 70+ averaged +7.0% over 60 sessions (1,406 results, 56% beat the index).

pead_parts.name: Profit surprise
pead_parts.rule: EBITDA change on the year against the spread of its last five yearly changes (standardised unexpected earnings): 1.0+ 2 · 0+ 1. Under 3 years of comparable history: EBITDA change of 3%+ of last year's revenue 2 · any rise 1.

pead_parts.name: Profit jump vs share price
pead_parts.rule: Rise in quarterly net profit on the year worth 0.5% or more of the market value before the result.

pead_parts.name: Revenue surprise
pead_parts.rule: Same test on revenue: 1.5+ 2 · 0+ 1. Short history: revenue growth 25%+ 2 · 8%+ 1.

pead_parts.name: Price reaction
pead_parts.rule: Return over the first two sessions after the result, minus NIFTY 500: +4% or more 2 · +1% or more 1.

pead_parts.name: Strong close
pead_parts.rule: Closed in the top 30% of the two sessions' high-low range.

pead_parts.name: Near the 52-week high
pead_parts.rule: Before the result the stock was within 10% of its 52-week closing high.

quality_parts.name: Revenue growth
quality_parts.rule: Revenue vs the same quarter last year (banks: net interest income). 50%+ 20 · 30%+ 18 · 20%+ 16 · 12%+ 13 · 6%+ 9 · up 5 · down up to 10% 2 · worse 0.

quality_parts.name: Operating profit growth
quality_parts.rule: EBITDA vs the same quarter last year (banks: operating profit before provisions). 40%+ 20 · 25%+ 17 · 15%+ 15 · 5%+ 11 · up 7 · down up to 15% 3. From a loss: back to profit 16, smaller loss 6.

quality_parts.name: Margins
quality_parts.rule: 10 if the margin is the highest of the last five quarters, plus the change on the year: +1 pt or more 10 · up 7 · down up to 1 pt 4 · down up to 3 pts 2.

quality_parts.name: Consistency
quality_parts.rule: Quarters in a row with operating profit up on the year: 1 = 8 · 2 = 11 · 3+ = 14. Plus revenue growth speeding up (3+ pts faster than last quarter) 6, or holding 3.

quality_parts.name: Clean profit
quality_parts.rule: Starts at 20. Net loss −10 · exceptional gain over 10% of PBT −5 · tax rate under 10% −4 · other income over 30% of PBT −4 (over 50% −6). 8 or less caps the score at 54 (WEAK).

data: Data: every quarterly result filed on NSE in XBRL from the June 2019 quarter on (Jul 2019 – Jul 2026 announcements), consolidated where the company files it; announcement dates from NSE's board-meeting records (the XBRL often arrives a day later); split-adjusted prices from Upstox. Returns start at the close of the second session after the result — what a buyer after the reaction would have got — minus NIFTY 500 over the same days. Included: price ₹20+, median turnover ₹1 Cr+ a day and market cap ₹300 Cr+ at the time; the extreme 0.5% of returns at each end trimmed.
caveats: Caveats: only companies listed today are in the data (delisted ones are missing), which flatters averages but affects every band alike. 2019–2026 was mostly a strong market for small and mid caps; 2025 was weak for all bands, but the ordering held. Thresholds were set on the whole sample and checked on each half separately. These are averages, not promises: about 4 in 10 high-score results still lagged the index. No costs or taxes.

sources.t: Post-earnings-announcement drift: overview (Ball & Brown 1968, Bernard & Thomas 1989)
Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok 1996 (earnings and price momentum)
Martineau 2022 (drift has faded in large US stocks)
